questions.q: Why filter data as early as possible in a query?
options: It reduces the rows later steps must process, and for foldable connectors can push the filter back to the source
It's required before you can set data types
It automatically renames the query
It only affects the final visual, not query performance
questions.explain: Fewer rows means less work for every step after the filter, and query folding can let the source database do the filtering instead of Power Query.

questions.q: Why should expensive operations like sorting come last in a query?
options: A sort must read the entire source before returning any rows, unlike a streaming operation like a filter
Sorting is only possible as the final step in Power Query
It has no effect on preview performance
Filters must always come after sorts
questions.explain: Sorting can't return partial results — it needs everything before it can know what's first. Streaming operations like filters return results as they go, so they belong earlier.

questions.q: Why does setting the correct data type on a column matter beyond just correctness?
options: It unlocks type-specific tools and filters, like date-specific options in the Add Column menu
It has no practical effect in Power Query
It's only relevant for numeric columns
It automatically fixes data quality errors
questions.explain: Type-specific transformations and filters (like previous-period date filters) stay grayed out until the column actually has the matching data type applied.

questions.q: What do Power Query's data profiling tools (Column quality, distribution, and profile) help you do?
options: See error/empty rates, value frequency, and detailed statistics before you start transforming data
Automatically merge two queries together
Rename applied steps
Connect to a new data source
questions.explain: Profiling surfaces data problems before you build transformations around them, so you catch quality issues early instead of after they've broken a step downstream.

questions.q: What does the Extract Previous option do?
options: Splits a query into two at the chosen step, turning everything before it into a new referenced query
Deletes every step before the selected one
Merges two separate queries into one
Extracts a single column into its own query
questions.explain: Extract Previous is used to break a long, hard-to-follow query into smaller, referenced pieces — useful right before a natural boundary like a merge step.
